AFBS.review: Attending his classes regularly is enough to do well.

MAR2.review: He is a great and exceptionally kind, wholesome faculty member.

SAMS.review: He makes history engaging and easy to remember. His exams are straightforward and partially marked; quizzes are easy, and lecture notes help with the short-answer and broad questions. He assigns a research-based paper and holds a brief viva. Attending and participating in class are important, so he may not suit students who cannot attend regularly.
A student described him as easygoing, with fair questions and good grading, and reported that a friend earned an A-.
Several students said he does not curve; one reported that friends repeatedly received A- grades without a curve.
One student felt his expectations were excessively demanding for a three-month course and said the grading was average, around B/B+.

SWH1.review: One student advised avoiding him. Another said he gives a question bank that exams draw from, with short questions in quizzes and the midterm, broad questions in the final, and a presentation.
A student said he causes a lot of stress, insults students, treats them like soldiers, and gives B+ grades.

MSIA.review: A student strongly advised against taking his class, saying it made their life miserable.
A student currently taking his class described him as excellent so far.

IZN.review: A student said exams use questions from the question bank, with short questions in quizzes and the midterm and broad questions in the final; the course also includes a presentation.

AFRN.review: He is humble, friendly, and easygoing. Exams are fairly easy; quizzes are multiple-choice, and he provides sample questions or suggestions for the midterm and final. He gives good marks, but his lectures can be boring and he was still new to teaching.
He is down-to-earth and grades fairly without bias, but the lectures are boring enough that students may need to study on their own.
He is easygoing and gives exam suggestions, with questions coming from them; quizzes and assignments are manageable, but he does not curve.
A student said he gives good grades, exam suggestions, and questions drawn from those suggestions, making it easy to earn marks, though the classes are boring.
One student found him easygoing but said the lectures were hard to understand and the grading was poor; the exam questions were posted online and repeated on the exams with many options.
A sarcastic comment implied his classes are so boring they could put someone to sleep.

SAR3.review: He teaches HIS103 through politics and international-relations perspectives, makes the classes interesting, and highlights important topics and dates in short slide decks. Memorizing the material is the main requirement.
A student described him as good and easygoing.

MBK1.review: His questions are straightforward and based on his slides. Quizzes are multiple-choice and the midterm is written; there is no presentation, but there is an assignment summarizing pages from a book. He is lenient and teaches well, though he does not curve.

FSY.review: She is friendly, teaches the material clearly, and uses her lessons for exam questions. Her quizzes use short, focused questions, and the slides are sufficient.
She teaches well and grades what students deserve. The course includes an individual poster presentation, and students can earn full marks on short questions by stating the main concepts.
Her slides are somewhat lengthy, but she repeats important topics and makes clear what to prioritize.

MBU.review: A student said he is a good person and that following his class and exam suggestions is the key to doing well; exam questions come from those suggestions.

MGRN.review: A student simply described him as the best.

TRH.review: A student said he gives fair grades.
A student described him as very easygoing.

AQR1.review: He is friendly, helpful, and down-to-earth, and tries to make a usually boring history course interactive. He assigns no extra burden and neither curves nor decurves; students receive what they earn.
A student said to follow his class carefully to do well.
A student described him as easygoing and among the best for marking and grading.

ZRS.review: Her midterms and final are easy, but her quizzes are very difficult and she does not curve.
